title: A-V-D
hook: avodah means both work and worship

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sh-M-R: shamar, to guard, the job in Eden and the word Cain refused. Your line was keep and guard. Did you keep the one promise? Today, the other half of that garden job. Day one thousand three hundred seventy-six.

Moses stands in front of Pharaoh with a message he will carry again and again. In the King James: "Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness." Serve. Strange word to bring to a king who already has the Hebrews building his store cities. The Hebrews are already serving every day: mud, straw, brick, field. Moses isn't asking for them to stop serving. He's asking for them to serve someone else. In Hebrew, the brickwork and the worship use the same root. That's the root for today.
screen: `LET MY PEOPLE GO.` → `THAT THEY MAY SERVE ME.` → `BRICKWORK AND WORSHIP: ONE ROOT.`

segments.voice: A-V-D. Ayin, vet, dalet. Avodah: work, labor, service, worship. Turn it four ways. First, back to yesterday's garden: "to dress it and to keep it." Keep was shamar. Dress is from this root: to work the soil, to till it. Before any altar or temple, avodah in the Eden story means digging. Second, Egypt. Early in Exodus comes a hard line: "they made their lives bitter with hard bondage." Bondage there is avodah. The same root names the worst thing in the story. Third, the way out. Let my people go, that they may serve me: serve is this root again. The exodus doesn't move the people from work to nothing. It moves their avodah from Pharaoh to God. And in Pirkei Avot, Shimon the Righteous teaches that the world stands on three things: Torah, avodah and acts of lovingkindness. Avodah there means the service in the Temple. Fourth, after the Temple. The rabbis read Deuteronomy's call "to serve him with all your heart" and ask what kind of service happens in the heart. Their answer, in tractate Taanit: prayer. Digging, slavery, offerings, prayer. One root runs through all of them. So the question the root keeps asking isn't whether you work. It's who and what the work is for.
screen: `TO DRESS IT: WORKING THE SOIL.` · `HARD BONDAGE IN EGYPT.` · `SERVE ME: THE SAME ROOT.` · `SERVICE OF THE HEART: PRAYER.` · then, large: `עֲבוֹדָה`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: dedicate one piece of work. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the next task waiting for you today: a spreadsheet, a load of laundry, a shift, a lesson plan, a diaper. Something ordinary. See yourself starting it. Now ask the root's question: who is this for? Maybe a customer, a child, a coworker who's tired, a stranger you'll never meet. Hold that person in mind, and let the task belong to them for a minute. If you pray, you can offer the work to God before you start. The bell holds the time.
A-V-D. Ayin, vet, dalet: avodah, the work of the soil, the bondage in Egypt, the Temple service, and prayer, the service of the heart. Today's word.
Your line: work is worship. Today, do that one task slowly and well, as if it were an offering, and notice who it was really for. Day one thousand three hundred seventy-six.

howItsDone: Jews call prayer avodah she-ba-lev, the service of the heart, after the rabbis' reading of Deuteronomy 11:13; on Yom Kippur the synagogue recalls the Temple's service in a section of prayers called the Avodah.

trapdoor: what you thought: work and worship are opposites, one for weekdays and one for holy days.
what it means: avodah is both: tilling the soil, the bondage in Egypt, the Temple service.
what a scholar hears: tractate Taanit reads 'to serve him with all your heart' as prayer, the service of the heart.

notes: Quotations from the KJV; confirm the Judaism path accepts KJV, or swap in JPS 1917 wording once verified.
Genesis 2:15 'dress' is l'ovdah, Exodus 1:14 'bondage' is ba'avodah, Exodus 7:16 'serve' is from the same root; confirm.
'He will carry again and again' refers to the repeated demand in Exodus 7–10; no count given.
Avot 1:2 (Shimon the Righteous: Torah, avodah, gemilut chasadim) paraphrased; the 'three things' count is in the Mishnah itself. Avodah glossed as the Temple service, the usual reading; confirm.
Taanit 2a: 'what is service of the heart? this is prayer', paraphrased.
howItsDone mentions the Yom Kippur Avodah section; confirm wording.
Editor: replaced 'whose whole kingdom runs on people serving' with the text's store cities (Exodus 1:11); cut the 'first avodah in the Torah' superlative.
